title: Residency fallback patterns + customer comm templates
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a small catalogue of fallback patterns for region-pin enforcement, operator steps for execution, and customer-facing communication templates for different classes of residency incidents. Goal is to provide lightweight, copy-pasteable guidance for oncall, solutions, and CSMs during outages or policy-triggered reprovisioning where strict region pinning cannot be honored immediately.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to Redwood Private and Dedicated customers with explicit region pins or contractual residency requirements.
- Does NOT replace full legal guidance — partner with Legal for escalations flagged as regulatory.
- Assumes platform can detect region pin violations (telemetry + audit evidence) and has the ability to switch routing at the tenant level.

Quick decision matrix (high level):
- Incident class A (Region unavailable for >5m and impacting >25% capacity): Immediate failover to customer-approved fallback region if SLA allows. Notify customer + create incident bridge.
- Incident class B (Transient routing mismatch <5m): Retry + KV cache flush; no customer-facing notice unless repeated.
- Incident class C (Policy/contract contradiction — enforcement blocked): Pause non-essential writes, escalate to Legal + Enterprise CS for approval, gather audit evidence.

Fallback patterns (concrete):
1) Soft-failover (preferred): Route read-only traffic to nearest compatible region; preserve writes in local queue with encryption-at-rest. Use this when contract allows temporary write buffering.
Operator steps:
  - Set tenant-routing-mode=soft-failover (API patch)
  - Enable metrics tag: residency.fallback=soft
  - Start storage-queue (ephemeral) and confirm encryption keys present
  - Monitor queue drain rate and latency SLOs

2) Hard-failover (only with explicit customer opt-in): Redirect all traffic to fallback region and mark events for audit. Use only when customer has signed fallback rider.
Operator steps:
  - Run migration-checklist: version-compat, kernel-compat, kv-schema-match
  - Toggle tenant-route and verify healthchecks in fallback cluster
  - Trigger telemetry: query=COUNT(residency.pin_mismatch) by tenant, window=1m

3) Scoped-exception (short-term legal-approved): Allow selective endpoints (embeddings only) to escape pin. Requires exception token and timebox.

Audit evidence checklist (minimal):
- Tenant ID, pinned-region, observed-region, timestamps (UTC)
- Request IDs and sample payloads (redact PII)
- Router logs and matching decision predicates
- Operator action log (who toggled flags)

Customer-facing templates (editable):
1) Short alert (email/portal banner) — incident class A:
Subject: Incident: temporary routing to alternate region for [customer-name]
Hi [Customer contact],
We detected a region service degradation in [pinned-region] affecting traffic to your dedicated environment. To maintain availability we have temporarily routed traffic to [fallback-region]. No customer data was shared outside your tenant boundary and all data remains encrypted. We expect to revert to your pinned region once health checks pass; we will update you at 30 minutes and again on resolution.
Actions we took: enabled soft-failover, started encrypted queue for writes, increased tracing.
Next steps: post-incident report with audit evidence and timeline.

2) Formal notice (policy exception required):
Subject: Request: permission to apply residency exception for [customer-name]
Hi [Legal/CS team],
We need expedited approval to apply a timeboxed exception for writes to flow to fallback-region for 4 hours to avoid data loss. Attached: audit samples and risk assessment. Please respond with approval token or request more detail.

Testing and validation playbook (SRE + Solutions):
- Pre-deploy checklist: confirm fallback-region matches runtime kernel version, quantization profile, and model artifact checksum.
- Chaos test run: scheduled canary where N% of tenants are toggled to soft-failover for 10 minutes; validate metrics and customer notification pipeline.
- Regression harness: include residency pinning tests in nightly integration (tokenized customers).

Telemetry queries (examples):
- Count mismatches: SELECT count(*) FROM router_logs WHERE event=residency_pin_mismatch AND tenant_id='T123' AND ts > now() - interval '15 minutes';
- Audit evidence search: grep router.log "tenant=T123" | head -n 200

Open questions / action items:
- (Priya) Draft legal-approved fallback rider template for sales to use — due 2025-03-12.
- (Samir) Add telemetry tag residency.enforcement_reason to all router responses — PR #1345.
- (Ellen) Build portal banner component for auto-notify when tenant-routing-mode changes.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a two-tier exception system: operational (<=2h auto-approve) vs legal (>2h manual).
- Could we allow per-endpoint pinning so customers can pin storage region but not inference? design question for product.

Appendix: quick command snippets
- Toggle soft-failover: curl -X PATCH https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/T123 -d '{"routing_mode":"soft-failover"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN"
- Generate audit bundle: /scripts/generate_residency_bundle.sh --tenant T123 --from 2025-03-02T08:00Z --to 2025-03-02T09:00Z

This is a working document: feel free to copy templates into customer messages, or propose changes inline.
